title: Verify the Grid Covers Every Facility
real_world_story: As the utility grows, it must guarantee that every facility remains connected to the main grid. A single traversal from the central substation can confirm whether the whole network is one connected region.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Substations and the transmission lines that connect them
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Checking that a single traversal reaches every facility

problem_statement: Given N substations numbered 0 to N-1 and E undirected transmission lines, starting a traversal from substation 0, determine whether every substation can be reached.
task: Print 1 if the entire grid is connected from substation 0, otherwise print 0.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and E. The next E lines each contain two integers u v describing an undirected transmission line between substations u and v.
output_format: Print 1 if all N substations are reachable from substation 0, otherwise print 0.

examples.explanation: Starting from substation 0, traversal reaches 1, 3 and 2, covering every facility.
Substation 4 is isolated, so not every facility can be reached from substation 0.

expected_algorithm.reason: A single BFS or DFS from the central substation visits every station in its connected component, so comparing the number of visited stations with N confirms full coverage.

hint: Traverse the graph starting from substation 0.
Count how many distinct stations are visited.
Compare the count with N to decide full connectivity.
real_world_takeaway: A single graph traversal can verify whether a large network is fully connected, which is a key reliability check as a power grid grows.
